headlines: Two independent 3D models agree. The square cantilever solved with a 3D solid (H27) and with a Lagrange beam (Q16 4x4 section) gives tip deflections that differ by 0.0004% and first frequencies by 0.0021%.

Taylor expansion up to order 20. TE20 reaches the 3D solid solution within 0.04% (tip deflection); the frequencies are within 0.85% of Timoshenko; the solution is independent of the section size (n up to 20, scaled geometry).

Patch tests. 68 uniform-extension tests (Taylor n = 1-20, all Lagrange sections, HQ4, plates, solids, mixed kinematics) reproduce the exact field; the largest error is 4.5e-14 (relative to the imposed displacement).
Pure bending. 24 checks of the exact quadratic solution (quadrilateral and T6 sections, Q9/Q16/T6 plates, H27 and H8+MITC solids) have a largest error of 1.0e-10.

HLE. HQ4 p = 1 coincides with Q4 (identical to the last printed digit); sub-elements of different order on the same interface satisfy the Ritz bounds and are independent of the node numbering (identical to the last printed digit); the curved tube with four HQ4 elements is within 1.13% of Timoshenko for p >= 4.

Plates. Navier plate within 0.26% (Q4, Q9, Q16 with MITC); cross-ply laminates within 0.79% of the closed form; Q9 plates with TE up to order 20 within 0.14% of the 3D solid; rotation of isotropic-equivalent plies exact to 2e-10.
Non-uniform kinematics. The ten pairs (TE-m/TE-n, TE/LE, HLE/TE, HLE/LE) are exact on the patch test and continuous at the interface (largest error 2.3e-08).

Multi-dimensional models. 1D/2D, 1D/3D and 2D/3D junctions reproduce the closed form to 8.3e-11; three regions of different dimension in one input equal the three separate runs (identical to the last printed digit).
MITC. On L/h = 100 structures the full integration gives 3-10% of the correct deflection for B2 beams, Q4 plates and H8 solids; MITC restores 94-99%.
